resources.string: Second screen for the AYN Thor
One tap: finds the PC on your network, works out which game it\'s running, and opens the second screen.
Set the address by hand, choose the display, and control how the screen behaves.
Needs the Ayn Dual Screen SMAPI mod. Network access is on by default; if it was turned off, set \"AllowLanAccess\": true in its config.json.
Needs the Ayn Dual Screen tModLoader mod. Network access is on by default; if it was turned off, re-enable AllowLanAccess in its mod config.

Needs the Ayn Dual Screen Forge mod for Minecraft 1.21.1. It uses port 27302 so it doesn\'t clash with the other two. Network access is on by default; if it was turned off, set allowLanAccess = true in config/ayndualscreen-client.toml.
Keep retrying when the game restarts. Off: drop straight back to the menu when the session ends.
Reopen on the same panel next time without asking.
Hold the screen on. Turning this off lets the panel dim normally.
Found %1$d. Tap one to use it.
Nothing found on port %1$d. Check the game is running with LAN access on, and that a VPN isn\'t in the way.
Connected to %1$s, but it\'s at the main menu. Load a save and the screen will fill in.
That address is running %1$s, not %2$s. Switch the game above, or check the address.
Something answered there, but it isn\'t one of the mods. %1$s
The PC is there, but nothing is listening on that port. %1$s is either not running, or the mod is still on localhost only — enable LAN access in the mod and restart the game.
That address doesn\'t resolve. Try the PC\'s numeric IP from \"ipconfig\" instead of its name.
No answer. The address may be on a different network, or Windows Firewall may be blocking the port — allow it for Private networks.

\"localhost\" means this device, not your PC — that\'s why it fails here. The mod prints that address for use on the PC itself. Enter the PC\'s network address instead, from \"ipconfig\" (it looks like 192.168.x.x).
Enter the PC\'s address first, or tap Find my PC.
The game session closed — back to the menu.
Couldn\'t get the session back — back to the menu.
Couldn\'t load the wiki. It needs an internet connection.

Needs the Ayn Dual Screen xNVSE plugin, and the game started through nvse_loader.exe rather than FalloutNV.exe — launched directly, the plugin never loads. It uses port 27303. Network access is on by default; if it was turned off, set AllowLanAccess=1 in Data\\NVSE\\Plugins\\AynDualScreen.ini. Tale of Two Wastelands works with the same plugin.
Any web page, opened full-screen with no browser chrome. Handy for a dashboard, a stream, or a wiki parked on the second display.
Looking for a game on your network…
No game found. Pick one and enter its address.
On launch, check the saved address and switch to whatever is actually running.
Experimental. These looks are unfinished and change how the whole app appears. Pick Ayn Dual Screen at any time to return to the standard look.
A theme is one small JSON file, plus a folder of PNG icons if you want them. Every field is optional. The quickest way to get files onto the device is this app\'s own FTP server.
Ready: %1$s\n\nexample.json and README.txt are in there. Copy the example, rename it, and it appears in this list.
Could not create the folder. Grant all-files access on the FTP screen first.
Not finished — the app can pair with a PC, but nothing decodes video yet.

Pairs this device with a PC running Sunshine or GeForce Experience. Pairing works and is remembered — but nothing decodes video yet, so there is no game to watch here. This is the groundwork, not the feature.
Paired — this PC knows this device.
Something is already streaming from this PC.
Sunshine shows a PIN page in its web interface. GeForce Experience pops up a box on the desktop.
Needs a companion program on the PC — not built yet.
Shares this device over the network so a PC can browse and copy its files, the way a homebrew FTP server does on a handheld console. Plain FTP, on your own network — no encryption.
Server is off. Start it, then type this address into your PC\'s file manager.
Start the server when the app opens
The server is not running. Go back and press Start server.
Go back, change the port if that is the problem, and try again. If this keeps happening, the message above is the exact reason — send it on.
The server is running, but this device has no address a PC could reach. Connect to Wi-Fi.
Anonymous — any username and password will do.
FTP sends the password in clear text. It is a doorlock for your own network, not a secret — don\'t reuse a real one.
Anything worth keeping to hand: seed numbers, boss order, a shopping list.
Applies while the app is open, and needs no permission.
Changes device brightness for everything. Needs the Modify System Settings permission.
Android has no public way to set two panels separately, so this moves both.
Every change lands here as you make it
A whole look in one tap. Everything below still works afterwards.
Hide the ones you never use. They stay off the home grid until you turn them back on.
Take this off the home grid? You can bring it back under Appearance → Tools shown.
Not enabled yet. Turn it on in the system keyboard list, then come back and switch to it.
Enabled, but not the one in use. Tap Switch to it and pick Thor Keyboard.
Active. It\'s the keyboard everything on this device now types with.
Split pushes the keys out to the edges, under your thumbs, the way a handheld wants them. Full width uses the whole row.
Type here with the keys below
Copies this device\'s main screen onto its second panel, and keeps going while you use other apps. It shows the Thor\'s own screen — not the PC\'s.
Mirroring. The second panel is showing this screen; stop it here or from the notification.
Ready. Android will ask you to confirm screen capture before it starts.
Screen capture was declined, so nothing is being mirrored.
No second display found. Plug one in, or open the Thor\'s second panel, then come back.
Needs permission to draw over other apps — that\'s what puts the picture on the second panel while you\'re in a game.
Floating buttons that stay on screen while you use other apps. Text and key macros go through the Thor Keyboard, so they land wherever you\'re typing — they can\'t reach a game\'s own controls.
Delete \"%1$s\" and every button in it?
This is the only profile left. Make another one first.
No buttons in this profile yet.
What it says on the button
Hidden. Show it and the buttons stay put while you use anything else.
On screen. Tap a button to fire it.
Moving. Drag the buttons where you want them — they save as you drop them.
Needs permission to draw over other apps, which is what keeps the buttons on screen outside this app.
Switch to the Thor Keyboard first — that\'s what puts the text in.
Couldn\'t find an app with package %1$s.
Tap Hide to put it away.
No notes yet. Tap New, or drop a .txt file into the notes folder over FTP.
Nothing on this device can take shared text.
app-private storage — grant All files access to reach them over FTP
Nothing in this room yet. Draw something and send it — it is kept even with nobody else here.
No saved connections yet. Scan the network to find one, or tap New to type an address.
Could not write the file. Grant All files access, or use Share.

Written to
%1$s

It is reachable over this app's FTP server.
Nothing in there could be read as a connection.
Something answered, but it is not a companion server.
Nothing is listening on that port. The mod may be bound to the PC only.
Only one connection can do this. Setting it here clears it elsewhere.
Needs a host and a port
Companion servers announce nothing, so this asks every address on your network whether the port is open. It cannot see past a router.
Nothing answered on %1$s. Check the PC is on the same network and the mod allows LAN access.
Port open, not a companion server
That screen went away. Back on the main display.
Show page controls in the session menu
No macros yet. Tap New to build one.
That macro has no steps yet.
Delete \"%1$s\"? Buttons that run it will stop working.
No steps yet. Tap Add step.
X, IN TENTHS OF A PERCENT
Y, IN TENTHS OF A PERCENT
Hold a key for a while
No second screen open, so there is nowhere to send that.
Drag a button to move it. Drag its corner to resize.
Tap holds the key down, tap again releases it
Replace this layout\'s buttons with the starting set?
Delete the layout \"%1$s\" and all its buttons?
This is the only layout, so it cannot be deleted.

Written to
%1$s

It carries the macros its buttons need.
That is not readable as JSON.
That file is not a layout.
That layout was made by a newer version of the app.
That layout has no buttons in it.
Everything here works without a game, a server or a network.
Switch to whichever companion is answering. Off: stay on the game you picked.
Asking the game what it offers…
Game codes are off for this game.
This game offers none. The mod may have them switched off.
Switching this off entirely hides the feature again and stops the app asking any game about codes.
Everything the app remembers, in one place.
Hide the tab until the code is entered again
Takes the tile away without switching game codes off. Your settings are kept.
Hidden. Enter the sequence again to bring it back.
This app installs from GitHub rather than a store, so this screen is how it stays current.
Updates come from github.com/%1$s. Downloads are checked against the digest GitHub holds, and installed by Android, not by this app.
You are on the latest version (%1$s).
Downloaded and checked. Android will ask you to confirm the install.
Downloaded and checked. Android needs your permission before this app can start an install.
This release came with no notes.

Android asks for this per app: it lets this app hand the downloaded file to the system installer, which is what actually installs it. You still confirm the install yourself, and you can turn it back off afterwards.
Runs in the background while the app opens, at most once every six hours. Off: nothing is checked unless you press the button above.
The abacus, for about two seconds when the app opens. Tap it to skip. Devices with system animations turned off never show it.
Includes pre-releases. Expect rough edges, and expect to report them.
No internet connection, so there was nothing to ask. Connect to Wi-Fi and try again.
Could not reach GitHub. The connection may have dropped, or a VPN or firewall may be in the way.
GitHub is rate-limiting this network. It allows 60 anonymous requests an hour and this address has used them; try again later.
The release could not be found. The repository may have been renamed or made private.
GitHub returned an error of its own. Nothing to fix at this end — try again later.
GitHub returned something this app could not read. Try again later.
The latest release carries no APK, so there is nothing to install from it.
The latest release does not say which app version it contains, so it cannot be compared with this one.
The download did not finish. Trying again continues from where it stopped.
Not enough free space on this device for the download.
The downloaded file does not match what GitHub says it published, so it was deleted rather than installed. Try again.
The downloaded file is not a readable APK, so it was deleted rather than installed.
That APK is a different app, so it was not installed.

That APK was signed with a different key than the copy you have installed. Android would refuse to install it over the top, and this app will not offer it. Install it by hand only if you know where it came from.
That release turned out not to be newer than what is installed.
Android has not been told this app may install apps. Grant it on the page below, then press Install again.
The installer could not be started. You can install the downloaded file yourself from a file manager.
Give the pad back to the game
The game keeps the controller. This screen still takes taps — it just no longer steals the buttons.
This screen has the controller now, so it can be typed into. The game will not respond to the pad until you hand it back.
Let the game keep the controller
Android gives one window the buttons at a time, across both panels. On: a second screen never takes them, so the game keeps responding while you use it. Off: the second screen can be typed into.
Some streams stay locked while Do Not Disturb is on.
Press buttons, move the sticks, swipe the screen. Whatever this device actually sends turns up below — which is the only way to tell why a control works on one handheld and not another.
The same watcher the home screen uses, so what it makes of your input is what the home screen would make of it.
Tools for working on this app on the device it runs on, rather than on the PC it was built on.

Lets a PC reach this device with adb without a cable — to install a build, read a log, or take a screenshot. This app cannot switch it on for you, and should not be able to: it is the switch that lets another machine on your network install software.
Android 11 and later give wireless debugging a new random port each time it is turned on. The number is on the Wireless debugging page, next to the pairing option.
5555 is the usual port once ADB over TCP is running.
USB debugging is off. Turn on Developer options, then USB debugging, then Wireless debugging.
USB debugging is on, but wireless debugging is not. Turn it on in Developer options to connect without a cable.
Wireless debugging is on. Pair the PC once from the Wireless debugging page, then connect with the command above.
No network address. Join a Wi-Fi network first.
This device has no settings page to open.
First time on this PC: pair

On the Wireless debugging page, tap "Pair device with pairing code". It shows a pairing port and a six-digit code — run the command with that port, then type the code. Once per PC, not once per session.
None of these are required. The second screen — the thing this app is for — works with all of them switched off. Each one turns on an optional tool, and skipping is a perfectly good answer.
This app has no accessibility service and asks for no location, camera, microphone or contacts access. You can change any of this later in Settings → Permissions.
Lets the FTP server, the screen mirror and the macro pad show that they are running — and each notification carries the Stop button that is the quickest way to end them.
Without it those tools still work; they just run without saying so, which Android otherwise requires them to do.
Lets the app hand a downloaded update to Android\'s installer, so a new version is one tap from the update screen.
It grants nothing by itself: you still confirm every install on Android\'s own screen. Without it, updates download and you install them by hand from a file manager.
The macro pad and the screen mirror, both of which exist to keep working after you leave this app for a game.
A powerful permission: an app that holds it can draw anything anywhere. This one draws the buttons you placed and the mirror you started, and nothing when both are off.
The FTP server, so a PC can browse this device the way homebrew file servers do, rather than a handful of media folders.

The broadest permission Android grants, and the reason this app is a sideloaded APK rather than a Play Store listing. Nothing else in the app reads it, and with the server off nothing reads it at all.
The system brightness slider on the Brightness screen.
Device-wide, because Android offers no way to dim one panel. Without it the app can still dim its own window, which needs no permission.
Stops the system dozing a long FTP transfer or a long mirroring session part way through.
Most people should skip this. It costs battery, and everything else in the app runs while you are looking at it.
%1$s is running, but it is at the main menu. Codes it lists may refuse until a save is loaded.
No saved connection answered as a running game. Start the game, or pick one below.
Show the tile without the sequence
The button sequence is still the way in, but it needs this handheld to report its d-pad in a way the app recognises. If it will not, this puts the tile on the home screen anyway.
